words.gram: verb, honorific -시- + polite imperative -어요, polite style (해요체)

meanings.note: Basic motion verb; in 안녕히 가세요 it bids farewell to someone leaving.
Used with destinations marked by -에 or -로.

examples.trans: I am going home now.
I have to go to school tomorrow.

related.gloss: to go and see / try going

가보다.gloss: to go and see; to visit

meanings.en: to go and check; to go see
meanings.note: Compound of 가다 ('to go') + 보다 ('to see/try').
Often used in past tense 가 봤다 for experiential meaning.

examples.trans: I'll have to go see for myself.
Have you ever been to Jeju Island?

meanings.note: In -(으)ㄴ/는/(으)ㄹ 것 같다, expresses supposition or soft assertion.

meanings.en: to be the same; to be like
meanings.note: Used with -와/과 or -랑 to compare two things.

examples.trans: It looks like it's going to rain.
Our thoughts are the same.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그 아이 ('that child/kid'); used only for younger people or close peers.

examples.trans: Are you close with her?
He is late every day.

related.gloss: this kid / he or she (near speaker)
that kid / he or she (over there)

meanings.note: Bound noun requiring a preceding modifier; often contracted to 거 in speech.
Forms grammatical patterns such as -ㄹ 것 같다 ('it seems') and -는 거지 ('it's that...').

examples.trans: This is my book.
We're meeting tomorrow, right?

meanings.en: to be curious; to wonder about
meanings.note: Descriptive adjective in Korean; the thing wondered about takes -이/가.

examples.trans: I'm really curious about the result.
If you have anything you're curious about, please ask.

meanings.en: just; simply; without any special reason
meanings.note: Very common conversational adverb.
Indicates leaving something in its current state.

examples.trans: I'll just stay home.
Why are you smiling? Just because.

그러다.gloss: to do so; to say so

meanings.en: to say so; to tell someone
meanings.note: Contraction of 그렇게 하다/말하다; often follows indirect quotations.

meanings.en: to do that; to act like that
meanings.note: Refers back to a previously mentioned action or state.

examples.trans: Tell them to come quickly.
What's wrong? / Why are you acting like that?

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그런데; introduces a contrast or obstacle.
Used to shift the topic in conversation.

examples.trans: By the way, what time is it now?
I want to go. But I don't have time.

meanings.note: Emphasizes necessity or strong intention.
Used with holding or closing actions.

examples.trans: Definitely contact me tomorrow.
Please close the door tightly.

까다롭다.gloss: to be picky; to be demanding

meanings.en: to be picky; fussy; hard to please
meanings.note: ㅂ-irregular adjective: 까다롭다 -> 까다로워.

meanings.en: to be strict; complicated (of rules or procedures)
meanings.note: Used for demanding requirements or conditions.

examples.trans: Our team leader is really picky.
The admission procedure is very strict.

meanings.note: Used with equals or younger people; becomes 내가 with subject particle -가 and 난 with topic particle -는.

examples.trans: I want to go together too.
I'll do it first.

meanings.note: Placed before time nouns like 주 ('week'), 달 ('month'), 날 ('day').
Used as a standalone noun, often with -에.

examples.trans: Let's meet again next week.
Please come again next time.

meanings.en: to be okay; to work; to suffice
meanings.note: In 안 되다, means 'won't do' or 'is not allowed'.
Auxiliary verb expressing obligation.
Takes -이/가 before 되다.

examples.trans: You must not take photos here.
We have to leave now.

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'rehearsal', commonly used in broadcasting and performing arts.

examples.trans: There is a rehearsal before the performance.
The rehearsal starts at 2 p.m.

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'main', used before nouns like 피디 ('PD') or 요리 ('dish').

examples.trans: Today's main dish is steak.
That person is the main writer of this program.

meanings.en: to be sorry; to feel apologetic
meanings.note: Descriptive adjective; used with peers or younger people (whereas 죄송하다 is honorific/humble).

examples.trans: I'm really sorry I'm late.

examples.text: 미안하지만 다시 한 번 말씀해 주세요.
examples.trans: I'm sorry, but please say that one more time.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 무엇; becomes 뭐가 with subject particle -가.

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
What is the most delicious?

보다.gloss: to see; to look; to view

meanings.en: to see; to watch; to look at
meanings.note: Basic perception verb.
In -기에 ('in one's view'), expresses perspective or judgment.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
In my view, it seems okay.

빼다.gloss: to take out; to remove; to exclude

meanings.en: to take out; to remove; to exclude
meanings.note: Used for removing someone from a schedule or taking something out.
Used in arithmetic.

examples.trans: Please take my name off the list.
I took the key out of my pocket.

meanings.en: to fight; to quarrel; to argue
meanings.note: The opponent takes -와/과 or -랑.

examples.trans: Do you fight with your younger sibling often?
Don't fight with each other and get along.

meanings.note: Short-form negation adverb placed directly before a verb or adjective.

examples.trans: I didn't drink coffee today.
This food is not spicy.

meanings.note: Used in set greetings such as 안녕히 가세요 ('Goodbye', to someone leaving) and 안녕히 계세요 ('Goodbye', to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!
Good night (sleep well).

meanings.note: Adverbial form of 어떻다; also used in rhetorical questions ('how could I...').

examples.trans: How did you get here?
How shall we solve this problem?

meanings.note: Colloquial intensifier (shortened from 엄청나게).

examples.trans: The weather is super cold today.
That movie was super fun.

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun for a location near the speaker.

examples.trans: Please sit here.
Please give me a glass of water here.

meanings.note: Kinship term used by females.

meanings.en: older male friend or colleague (used by a female)
meanings.note: Commonly used in Korea to address a close older male acquaintance or coworker.

examples.trans: I have one older brother.
Oppa, do you have time right now?

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 이것.

examples.trans: How much is this?
Please hold this for a moment.

meanings.note: Used for clothing worn on the body (shirts, pants, dresses, outfits).

examples.trans: I wore a black coat today.
It's cold, so please dress warmly.

meanings.note: Humble 1st person plural pronoun used when speaking to superiors or in formal settings.

examples.trans: We will prepare first.
Welcome to our company.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean noun used in 다음 주 ('next week'), 이번 주 ('this week'), 지난주 ('last week').

examples.trans: There is a meeting this Friday.
I exercise three times a week.

meanings.note: Indicates doing something personally without an intermediary.

examples.trans: Did you make this cake yourself?
Let's meet in person tomorrow and talk.

meanings.note: Very common colloquial adverb (also used as a noun meaning 'the real thing').

examples.trans: I was really busy today.
Is that story true?

meanings.note: Korean broadcasting abbreviation for 'producer-director', spelled in Hangul as 피디 or in English as PD.

examples.trans: Who is the main PD of that drama?
The PD directs the filming set.

meanings.note: 피디 + honorific suffix -님, used when addressing or referring respectfully to a producer-director.

examples.trans: PD, may I speak with you for a moment?
The PD is in a meeting right now.

meanings.en: to scold; to reprimand; to tell off
meanings.note: Transitive verb (contraction of 혼을 내다); passive/intransitive counterpart is 혼나다.

examples.trans: Mother scolded my younger sibling.
Don't scold the children too harshly.
